name: Treaty with the Piankashaw, 1805
aka: Treaty of Vincennes with the Piankeshaw, December 30, 1805
nations: Piankeshaw (now part of the Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma)
promises: The United States took the Piankeshaw under its 'immediate care and patronage' with protection as effectual as that given the Kaskaskia (Article 2).
An additional permanent annuity of $300 a year, plus $1,100 delivered at signing (Articles 3 and 4).
The right to live and hunt on the ceded lands as long as they remained United States property, and a reserved tract of 1,280 acres held in fee forever (Article 5).

breaches.what: The Indian Claims Commission found that the 2,622,000 acres ceded under this treaty (Royce Area 63, southeastern Illinois) were worth $1.25 an acre on 23 May 1807, against a consideration worth $7,100 (the $1,100 payment and the $300 annuity commuted at $6,000), and held that consideration unconscionable. It found the Piankeshaw entitled to $3,277,500 less the $7,100 credit.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Indian Claims Commission, Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma on behalf of the Piankeshaw Nation v. United States, Docket 99, Supplemental Findings of Fact of 5 December 1969 (22 Ind. Cl. Comm. 186)

breaches.quote: The Commission concludes that the value of the consideration for Royce Area 63 was unconscionable

breaches.what: The Commission entered a final award of $3,270,400 to the Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma on behalf of the Piankeshaw Nation.

landTaken: Royce Area 63, 2,622,000 acres in the Wabash valley in southeastern Illinois (Docket 99 supplemental findings, 1969).
compensation: $1,100 at signing and a permanent $300 annuity, valued together by the Commission at $7,100. Final award of $3,270,400 in 1970, with the United States reserving the right to claim offsets for gratuities after 23 May 1807.
today: In earlier findings (Docket 99, 1966) the Commission held the Piankeshaw had recognized title to the whole area, so they did not have to prove aboriginal occupancy.

nationVoice.nation: Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma
nationVoice.summary: The Tribe's history says the Piankashaw ceded their lands between the Wabash and the 1803 Kaskaskia cession in this 1805 treaty, quoting its first article, after which most Piankashaw joined the Kaskaskia, Wea and Peoria near Ste. Genevieve before removal to Kansas in 1832.

openQuestions: The Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma website (peoriatribe.com) has no history page on this treaty; a nation statement is still wanted.
What became of the 1,280-acre fee tract reserved by Article 5 was not researched.
The queue also lists the Miami Tribe of Oklahoma for this entry; the ICC award ran to the Peoria Tribe on behalf of the Piankeshaw.
